questions.subject: India History
questions.question: Which Mauryan ruler issued the 'Edict of Kalinga' expressing remorse after the devastating Kalinga War?
questions.explanation: Emperor Ashoka fought the Kalinga War around 261 BCE and was so horrified by the bloodshed that he issued edicts expressing deep remorse and subsequently embraced the path of Dhamma (non-violence and moral conduct).

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: The 'Din-i-Ilahi', a syncretic religious order blending elements of Islam, Hinduism, Zoroastrianism and other faiths, was founded by which Mughal emperor?
questions.explanation: Akbar founded the Din-i-Ilahi in 1582 CE as a syncretic religious movement aimed at promoting harmony among different religions. Birbal was among the very few Hindus who accepted it.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: The Dandi March of 1930 was undertaken to protest against which British law?
questions.explanation: Mahatma Gandhi led the Dandi March from 12 March to 6 April 1930, walking about 385 km from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi (Gujarat) to break the British Salt Law, thus launching the Civil Disobedience Movement.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: The 'Allahabad Pillar Inscription' (Prayag Prashasti), which provides detailed information about the conquests and administration of the Gupta king Samudragupta, was composed by which court poet?
questions.explanation: The Prayag Prashasti was composed by Harisena, who was a court poet and minister (mahadandanayaka) of Samudragupta. It is inscribed on the Ashokan pillar at Allahabad and is a key historical source for the Gupta era.

questions.subject: India History
questions.question: Which among the following was the immediate cause of the Revolt of 1857?
questions.explanation: The immediate cause of the 1857 revolt was the introduction of new Enfield rifle cartridges rumoured to be greased with cow and pig fat, which deeply offended both Hindu and Muslim sepoys who had to bite them open before loading.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the Non-Cooperation Movement formally adopted as a resolution in 1920?
questions.explanation: The Non-Cooperation Movement was first adopted at the special session of the INC held in Calcutta in September 1920, and then confirmed at the Nagpur Session in December 1920.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: The 'Quit India' resolution was passed by the All India Congress Committee (AICC) on 8 August 1942 at which city?
questions.explanation: The historic Quit India resolution was passed by the AICC at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Bombay (now Mumbai) on 8 August 1942, after which Gandhi gave the call of 'Do or Die'.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev were executed on 23 March 1931 in connection with the killing of which British police officer?
questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh and Rajguru shot John Saunders, a British police officer in Lahore, on 17 December 1928, to avenge the death of Lala Lajpat Rai. All three were hanged on 23 March 1931.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi started the famous Dandi March on 12 March 1930 from which ashram?
questions.explanation: Gandhi began the Salt March (Dandi March) from Sabarmati Ashram in Ahmedabad on 12 March 1930 and reached Dandi on 6 April 1930, where he broke the salt law.

questions.subject: Indian National Movement
questions.question: The Mountbatten Plan of June 1947, which proposed the partition of India, is also known by which other name?
questions.explanation: The Mountbatten Plan announced on 3 June 1947 is commonly referred to as the '3 June Plan'. It outlined the partition of British India into two independent dominions ? India and Pakistan.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The river Chambal originates from which of the following mountain ranges?
questions.explanation: The Chambal River originates from Janapav Hill in the Vindhya Range near Mhow in Madhya Pradesh and flows northward before joining the Yamuna.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which type of soil is most widely found in the Deccan Plateau region of India and is known for its high water-retention capacity?
questions.explanation: Black cotton soil (Regur soil) is predominantly found in the Deccan Plateau. It is formed from volcanic basalt rock, has high clay content, and retains moisture for a long time, making it ideal for cotton cultivation.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following Indian states receives rainfall primarily due to the retreating northeast monsoon (October?December)?
questions.explanation: Tamil Nadu receives most of its annual rainfall during October to December from the retreating northeast monsoon, because it lies on the eastern (Coromandel) coast which faces winds blowing from the Bay of Bengal at that time.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: The 'Great Barrier Reef', the world's largest coral reef system, is located along the coast of which country?
questions.explanation: The Great Barrier Reef is located off the northeastern coast of Australia in the Coral Sea. It is the world's largest coral reef system and is listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.question: Which of the following Indian states is the largest producer of groundnut in India?
questions.explanation: Gujarat is consistently the largest producer of groundnut in India, contributing the highest share of national groundnut production. Groundnut thrives in Gujarat's sandy loam soils and semi-arid climate.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which Five Year Plan in India adopted the 'Mahalanobis Model' as its strategic framework, emphasizing heavy industries and capital goods?
questions.explanation: The Second Five Year Plan (1956?61), drafted under the guidance of statistician P.C. Mahalanobis, prioritized rapid industrialization with a focus on heavy and capital goods industries.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: The 'Narasimham Committee' set up in 1991 was primarily associated with reforms in which sector of the Indian economy?
questions.explanation: The Narasimham Committee (1991), chaired by M. Narasimham, was appointed to examine the structure, organisation, and functioning of the financial and banking system in India and recommend reforms.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: Which type of unemployment is most commonly found among agricultural workers in India, where people appear to be employed but their marginal productivity is zero or near zero?
questions.explanation: Disguised unemployment refers to a situation where more people are employed in a job than actually required; their removal would not reduce total output, making their marginal productivity zero ? a common feature of Indian agriculture.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: If the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of a country is Rs. 500 crore and the depreciation of capital is Rs. 50 crore, what will be the Net Domestic Product (NDP)?
questions.explanation: NDP = GDP minus Depreciation. Here, NDP = 500 - 50 = Rs. 450 crore. Depreciation (also called Capital Consumption Allowance) is subtracted from GDP to arrive at NDP.

questions.subject: Indian Economy
questions.question: The 'Green Revolution' in India during the 1960s was most significantly associated with the introduction of High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds of which crop?
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution in India was primarily driven by the introduction of HYV seeds of wheat (notably developed by Norman Borlaug) and rice, which dramatically increased food grain production in states like Punjab, Haryana, and western UP.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: Under which Article of the Indian Constitution is the Right to Constitutional Remedies guaranteed, which Dr. B.R. Ambedkar called the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Article 32 of the Constitution guarantees the Right to Constitutional Remedies, empowering citizens to approach the Supreme Court for enforcement of Fundamental Rights. Dr. Ambedkar described it as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Directive Principles of State Policy are enshrined in Part IV of the Indian Constitution, covering Articles 36 to 51. These are non-justiciable guidelines for the State to keep in mind while framing policies and laws.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: Which house of the Indian Parliament is described as a permanent body that cannot be dissolved, and one-third of its members retire every two years?
questions.explanation: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent house and cannot be dissolved. Its members serve a six-year term and one-third of the members retire every two years, ensuring continuity of the upper house.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: By which Constitutional Amendment Act were the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens added to the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 added Part IVA (Article 51A) to the Constitution, incorporating ten Fundamental Duties of citizens on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.

questions.subject: Indian Constitution & Public Administration
questions.question: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions, added which Schedule to the Constitution dealing with powers and functions of Panchayats?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment Act added the 11th Schedule to the Constitution, which contains 29 subjects over which Panchayats can be given powers and responsibilities by the State Legislature.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which of the following enzymes is responsible for converting starch into maltose during digestion in the mouth?
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase (ptyalin), secreted by the salivary glands, breaks down starch into maltose in the mouth. Pepsin and trypsin act on proteins, while lipase acts on fats.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A person suffering from myopia (short-sightedness) needs which type of lens to correct his vision?
questions.explanation: In myopia, the image forms in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens is used to correct this defect as it diverges the incoming light rays so the image falls exactly on the retina.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: Which gas is produced when baking soda (sodium bicarbonate) is heated?
questions.explanation: When sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) is heated, it decomposes to produce sodium carbonate, water, and carbon dioxide gas. This reaction is: 2NaHCO3 ? Na2CO3 + H2O + CO2.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: In plants, which tissue is primarily responsible for the transport of water and dissolved minerals from roots to leaves?
questions.explanation: Xylem is the vascular tissue that conducts water and dissolved minerals upward from the roots to the rest of the plant. Phloem, in contrast, transports prepared food (sugars) from leaves to other parts.

questions.subject: General Science
questions.question: A circuit has three resistors of 6 ohm each connected in parallel. What is the equivalent resistance of this combination?
questions.explanation: For resistors in parallel, 1/R = 1/6 + 1/6 + 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2, so R = 2 ohm. In a parallel combination of identical resistors, the equivalent resistance equals one resistor's value divided by the number of resistors.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: A shopkeeper marks the price of an article 25% above its cost price and then offers a discount of 10% on the marked price. What is his profit percentage?

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: A sum of money doubles itself in 8 years at simple interest. In how many years will it become four times itself at the same rate of interest?
questions.explanation: If principal doubles in 8 years, SI earned = P in 8 years, so Rate = 100/8 = 12.5% per year. To become 4 times, SI needed = 3P. Time = (3P ? 100)/(P ? 12.5) = 24 years.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5. If 6 is added to each number, the new ratio becomes 3 : 4. What is the larger of the two original numbers?
questions.explanation: Let the numbers be 3x and 5x. Then (3x + 6)/(5x + 6) = 3/4. Cross-multiplying: 12x + 24 = 15x + 18, so 3x = 6, x = 2. The larger number = 5x = 10.

questions.subject: Elementary Arithmetic
questions.question: A can complete a piece of work in 12 days and B can complete the same work in 18 days. They work together for 4 days and then A leaves. In how many more days will B alone finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation: A's 1-day work = 1/12, B's 1-day work = 1/18. Together in 1 day = 1/12 + 1/18 = 5/36. In 4 days together = 20/36 = 5/9. Remaining work = 1 - 5/9 = 4/9. B alone takes 4/9 ? 18 = 8 days.

questions.question: Which type of Sandhi is formed in the word '??????' (Maharshi)?
questions.explanation: ??????' is formed from '??? + ???'. Here '? + ? = ???' which follows the rule of Gunn Sandhi (???? ????), where '?/?' followed by '?' gives '???'.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: In which Samas (compound) is the first word (Purvpad) dominant?
questions.explanation: In Avyayibhav Samas, the first word (Purvpad) is an indeclinable (Avyaya) and is dominant. The whole compound functions as an indeclinable. Example: '????????' (yathashakti).

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: What is the correct meaning of the idiom '????? ??? ??? ??????'?
questions.explanation: The idiom '????? ??? ??? ??????' means to deceive or mislead someone, i.e., '???? ????'. It refers to blinding someone's judgment by throwing dust in their eyes.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: What is the correct antonym (Vilom) of the word '?????'?
questions.explanation: ?????' means gentle, calm, or mild in nature. Its antonym is '????', which means fierce, aggressive, or intense. '????' and '?????' are near-synonyms of '?????', not antonyms.

questions.subject: General Hindi
questions.question: What is the Sthayi Bhava (permanent emotional state) of 'Veer Ras' (Heroic Sentiment)?
questions.explanation: The Sthayi Bhava of 'Veer Ras' is '??????' (enthusiasm/zeal). '?????' is the Sthayi Bhava of Raudra Ras, '??' of Bhayanak Ras, and '??????' of Adbhut Ras.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning to the word 'OBSTINATE'.
questions.explanation: Obstinate' means refusing to change one's opinion or course of action; 'Stubborn' is its closest synonym. 'Flexible', 'Timid', and 'Careless' carry entirely different meanings.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Choose the word most nearly opposite in meaning to the word 'FRUGAL'.
questions.explanation: Frugal' means careful and sparing with money or resources. Its antonym is 'Extravagant', meaning spending excessively. 'Thrifty' is actually a synonym, while 'Modest' and 'Cautious' do not convey the opposite meaning.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Select the most appropriate word to fill in the blank: The judge remained ______ throughout the trial, listening to both sides without showing any bias.
questions.explanation: Impartial' means treating all sides equally and fairly, which fits the context of a judge listening without bias. 'Partial' means biased, 'Emotional' is unsuitable in a judicial context, and 'Indifferent' implies lack of interest rather than fairness.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Each sentence below is divided into four parts (A), (B), (C), and (D). Find the part that contains a grammatical error: (A) She is one of / (B) the most talented student / (C) who has ever / (D) joined this institution.
questions.explanation: The phrase 'one of' must always be followed by a plural noun. So 'student' should be changed to 'students'. The correct form is 'one of the most talented students'.

questions.subject: General English
questions.question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: 'To burn the midnight oil'.
options: To work or study late into the night
questions.explanation: The idiom 'to burn the midnight oil' means to work or study until very late at night, originating from the days when oil lamps were used for late-night work. The other options do not match this meaning.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: In a certain code language, 'ORANGE' is written as 'PSBOHF'. Following the same rule, how will 'MANGO' be written in that code?
questions.explanation: Each letter is shifted one place forward: O?P, R?S, A?B, N?O, G?H, E?F. Similarly, M?N, A?B, N?O, G?H, O?P, giving NBOHP.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: Pointing to a woman in a photograph, Suresh said, 'She is the mother of my son's wife.' How is that woman related to Suresh?
questions.explanation: Suresh's son's wife is his daughter-in-law. The mother of his daughter-in-law is Suresh's son's mother-in-law, which makes her Suresh's co-in-law ? commonly termed 'mother-in-law' in the context of their children's marriage, i.e., his son's mother-in-law.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: Ramesh starts from point A and walks 8 km towards the North. He then turns right and walks 6 km. After that, he turns right again and walks 8 km. How far is he from point A, and in which direction?
questions.explanation: Ramesh walks North 8 km, then East 6 km (right turn), then South 8 km (right turn). The northward and southward distances cancel out. He is left 6 km to the East of point A.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: Statements: All chairs are tables. Some tables are desks. Conclusions: I. Some chairs are desks. II. Some desks are tables. Which conclusion(s) follow(s)?
questions.explanation: From 'Some tables are desks,' the converse 'Some desks are tables' is valid ? so Conclusion II follows. Conclusion I ('Some chairs are desks') cannot be established because the 'some tables' that are desks may not overlap with the chairs that are tables.

questions.subject: Logic & Reasoning
questions.question: Find the missing number in the series: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ?
questions.explanation: Each term follows the pattern: next term = (current term ? 2) + 1. So 3?2+1=7, 7?2+1=15, 15?2+1=31, 31?2+1=63, and 63?2+1=127.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Which Indian athlete won the gold medal in the javelin throw event at the 2023 World Athletics Championships held in Budapest, Hungary?
questions.explanation: Neeraj Chopra won the gold medal in javelin throw at the 2023 World Athletics Championships in Budapest, becoming the first Indian to win this title. He threw a distance of 88.17 metres in the final.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: The Indian government launched the 'PM Vishwakarma' scheme primarily to benefit which section of society?
questions.explanation: The PM Vishwakarma scheme was launched on 17 September 2023 to provide support to traditional artisans and craftspeople such as blacksmiths, carpenters, potters, weavers, and others who work with their hands and tools.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: India assumed the presidency of which major international grouping in December 2022 and hosted its summit in New Delhi in September 2023?
questions.explanation: India held the G20 Presidency from December 1, 2022, to November 30, 2023, and successfully hosted the G20 Leaders Summit in New Delhi on September 9-10, 2023, under the theme 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam'.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: India's Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully landed its lander 'Vikram' near the south pole of the Moon in August 2023. What was the name of the rover deployed from this lander?
questions.explanation: The Chandrayaan-3 lander 'Vikram' successfully soft-landed on the Moon on August 23, 2023, and deployed the rover named 'Pragyan', making India the first country to land near the lunar south pole.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Who was appointed as the Chief Election Commissioner of India in March 2024, succeeding Rajiv Kumar who retired from the post?
questions.explanation: Gyanesh Kumar was appointed as the Chief Election Commissioner of India in March 2024 after the retirement of Rajiv Kumar. He was selected under the new process introduced by the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Which Indian scientist was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024, recognized for his foundational contributions to India's space and missile programmes?
questions.explanation: APJ Abdul Kalam, known as the 'Missile Man of India', was awarded the Bharat Ratna posthumously in 2024. He made landmark contributions to India's PSLV and Agni missile programmes.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: India assumed the Presidency of which major international grouping in December 2022, hosting the G20 Summit in New Delhi in September 2023?
questions.explanation: India held the Presidency of G20 from December 1, 2022 to November 30, 2023, and hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit in New Delhi on September 9-10, 2023. The theme was 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam'.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: At the 2023 ICC Cricket World Cup held in India, which team defeated India in the final match to win the championship?
questions.explanation: Australia defeated India by 6 wickets in the final of the 2023 ICC Cricket World Cup played at Narendra Modi Stadium, Ahmedabad on November 19, 2023, to win their sixth World Cup title.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: Under which government scheme are eligible beneficiaries in India provided free food grains ? 5 kg per person per month ? which was extended up to December 2028?
options: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana
questions.explanation: Pradhan Mantri Garib Kalyan Anna Yojana (PMGKAY) provides 5 kg of free food grains per person per month to about 80 crore beneficiaries. The government announced its extension until December 2028.

questions.subject: Current Affairs
questions.question: India's Chandrayaan-3 mission successfully landed its Vikram lander near the south pole of the Moon in August 2023. Which Indian space agency conducted this mission?
questions.explanation: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) conducted the Chandrayaan-3 mission. The Vikram lander touched down near the lunar south pole on August 23, 2023, making India the first country to achieve a soft landing in that region.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The Revolt of 1857 is also known as:
questions.explanation: The Revolt of 1857 is described as the 'First War of Indian Independence' by some historians and as the 'Sepoy Mutiny' by British historians. Both terms are commonly used.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The concept of 'Judicial Review' in the Indian Constitution is borrowed from which country?
questions.explanation: The concept of Judicial Review is borrowed from the USA, where the Supreme Court has the power to review the constitutionality of laws.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The 'Palk Strait' separates India from which country?
questions.explanation: The Palk Strait is a narrow strip of water that separates Tamil Nadu (India) from the Northern Province of Sri Lanka.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The 'Finance Commission' of India is constituted under which Article of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: The Finance Commission is constituted under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution every five years to recommend the distribution of tax revenues between the Centre and States.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Which vitamin is essential for blood clotting?
questions.explanation: Vitamin K is essential for blood clotting (coagulation). It helps in the synthesis of prothrombin in the liver.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The famous 'Ajanta Caves' are known for:
questions.explanation: The Ajanta Caves are famous for their Buddhist rock-cut cave paintings and sculptures, depicting the life of Buddha and Jataka tales.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The book 'The White Tiger' is written by:
questions.explanation: The White Tiger' is a novel by Aravind Adiga, published in 2008. It won the Man Booker Prize the same year.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in which city?
questions.explanation: The 2024 Summer Olympics were held in Paris, France, from 26 July to 11 August 2024.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: Who is the current President of India as of August 2026?
questions.explanation: Droupadi Murmu is the current President of India, having assumed office on 25 July 2022. She is the first tribal woman to hold this position.

questions.subject: General Awareness
questions.question: National Youth Day is celebrated in India on which date?
questions.explanation: National Youth Day is celebrated on 12 January every year to commemorate the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda.
